cards.name: Police pursuit + wanted level
cards.desc:
Wanted stars and a pursuit of up to 3 cop cars, as a free-roam consequence of bad driving — deliberately never a mission.

The hardest bug of the project: cops would not chase. **Six stacked causes.** Ended by *reconfiguring* rather than debugging further — all street-graph routing was deleted (police.ts 800 → 686 lines) so cops simply drive straight at the player, and they spawn near the player when the station is far.

The real physical blocker was found only by building a headless Rapier repro against the actual GLBs: a **zero-thickness painted lane sheet** whose edge, inside the character controller's skin, read as a 60.7° wall.

Escape model settled 2026-08-02: break line of sight and you're clear in 12/17/23 s by star level, or stop committing crimes and a hard cap clears you in 45/70/95 s. Invariant: no stars ⇒ no cops.

cards.name: Mission lifecycle, retry and briefings
cards.desc:
The pass that made the campaign survive being played, found by actually playtesting it end-to-end:

· The helicopter rescue could sample **zero** rooftop spots, making completion unreachable and the run a guaranteed timeout.
· `MissionHandle` gained `cleanup?()`, called on the completion edge — finished missions had been leaving delivered pedestrians, rescued survivors and 9 buoys plus their Rapier colliders in the world forever.
· The pizza `T` gate excluded `failed`, so a retry played the whole briefing, fade and teleport and then spawned nothing.
· Retry keys collided: `R` fired while in the helicopter/jetski (both poll it for respawn), and chase retry `F` didn't work on foot — a beach timeout meant swimming back out.
· Missions 3 and 4 got briefing cards. Mission 4's copy already existed in `chase.config.ts` and had **never been rendered**.

cards.name: Carjacking — steal any stopped traffic car
cards.desc:
`E` steals any **stopped** ambient traffic car anywhere in the city — the street twin of the parking-lot promotion path: `traffic.claim(id)` → `transitions.hijackTrafficCar`.

Design calls: the car waits 5 s for you · the simulation slot is **recycled** far away rather than retired (a car's id is its index in `cars[]`, so pushing a new one would corrupt it) · no wanted level for the theft.

Also fixed here: `player.setSolid()`, because the walking capsule had been staying solid but un-ticked in the lane while you drove — an invisible wall in traffic.

cards.name: Run over pedestrians + blood VFX
cards.desc:
Hit a pedestrian at ≥12 km/h and they're launched, land, lie, fade — and then that same person walks back onto their sidewalk. Recovery is free because `pedestrian.ts` keeps its own position and rewrites the transform once it's ticked again.

Motion model: the animation clip's **root motion is the knockback**; code adds only the vertical arc, since the clip's own vertical is flat. Blood spray plus a ground stain whose lifetime is *derived from the body's timeline*, so a stain can't outlive its victim.

Reliability fix the same day: the pedestrian capsule (0.3) plus the controller skin parked the vehicle exactly on a strict inequality boundary, making head-on hits a coin flip and bike hits impossible. Solved with Rapier interaction groups ghosting pedestrians above 12 km/h.

Tuned live on `/runover-test.html`.

Impact now plays a scream drawn from a male or female pool plus a synthesised body thud. Six CC0 clips, credited in `public/audio/sfx/CREDITS.md`.

cards.name: 🔀 Engine pivot #3: Three.js → Unity 6 (URP)
cards.desc:
**The project moved engines a third time, and this one stuck.** The shipped Three.js game becomes the *spec* and Unity 6000.5.8f1 (URP) rebuilds it — to learn a second engine and to use the advantages the web build had to work around.

**2026-08-16 this stopped being a side project: the Unity build is what gets submitted, with a 1 Oct 2026 deadline.** Every gap against the web build became a graded decision rather than a nice-to-have, and the deliverable stopped being only the game.

The instructor is invited to **both** repos, so the pivot is presented rather than hidden:

- Phase 1 — https://github.com/RoeeSivan/Finalproject
- Phase 2 — https://github.com/RoeeSivan/theblock-unity

Note the irony one column to the right: `❌ Engine: Unity` was abandoned on day one of this project, in April, for tooling friction. It came back in August because this time there was a finished game to port.

cards.name: U3 — Handedness: the `Convert` helper, negate X
cards.desc:
Three.js is right-handed Y-up; Unity is **left-handed** Y-up. glTFast negates **X** on import and passes Y and Z through.

So: `Convert.Pos(p) => (-p.x, p.y, p.z)` and `Convert.Yaw(y) => -y`, in **one static helper, one place — never an inlined sign flip**. The importer flips mesh data, but every hand-authored number in `config.ts` (district offsets, spawns, road polylines, waypoints, POIs) does not flip itself, and missing one mirrors that thing against everything else so it looks *almost* right.

Verified 8/8 against the placed scene objects, not assumed. `Assets/Scripts/Core/Convert.cs`.

cards.name: U4 + U5 — The offline pipeline: `export-config.mjs` → `WorldBuilder`
cards.desc:
**The arrow this port is proudest of, and it has no counterpart in the original.** `config.ts` → `export-config.mjs` → `theblock-config.json` → `WorldBuilder` (Editor) → baked `ScriptableObject`s. The runtime casts no rays for any of it.

This is also the **only** change the Three.js repo ever receives, so the exporter emits the **whole** config rather than a subset — a subset would have forced re-editing the original at U12, U13 and U17. 61 KB, byte-identical across runs, zero dependencies (Node 22 strips TypeScript types natively).

`WorldBuilder` is menu **The Block → Build World**. User-confirmed 2026-08-13: the user's own run reproduced the report line for line — 9 placed, 4 missing, 96 colliders.

cards.name: U11 — All 9 districts render clean
cards.desc:
Placement shipped in U5; this is the three rendering faults that survived it.

**Foliage:** the white shards were a spurious V flip in glTFast's `_ST`, not the blend mode, plus a real alpha-clip pass that rebinds to generated URP/Lit materials because `_AlphaClip` on an imported glTFast material is inert.

**Cities 2/3:** the baked-in parked cars are cut out at the **submesh** level at build time — 86% of the mesh — out of collision as well as sight. The web build has no edit-time step that could do this.

**Caught:** a substring pattern list that alpha-clipped every road, because "tree" is inside "CityGen_Streets". User-confirmed 2026-08-15.

cards.name: U12 — Roads on splines, ground, sea
cards.desc:
Roads are `com.unity.splines` + a generated ribbon, **not** the web's per-segment stretched tile: 1864 m of spline against 1859.5 m of polyline, corners actually curved, markings continuous through them. The `SplineContainer`s survive as U17's and U19's centreline.

Sea is `sea-surface.ts` ported into `Assets/Shaders/{Water,Beach}.shader` — URP ships no water — unlit on purpose, since the original does its own lighting. The beach is a displaced MeshCollider you walk down.

**Two faults found at U15's play-test and fixed:** `config.fog` was never ported, so the 320 m far plane sliced the skyline (the far plane, the fog and the background colour are one mechanism); and the ground plate showed through the sea's wave troughs — 0.37 m of swell against a plate at −0.05 m — so the plate is cut out under the water.

cards.name: U13 — Places: pizzeria + interior, gas station, police station, 101 lot cars
cards.desc:
User-confirmed 2026-08-15.

The gas station imported Y/Z swapped, because a Sketchfab export's cancelling root matrices do **not** cancel through glTFast; fixed by an `Rx(-90)` in `AssetAliases`, which can now correct the real asset instead of only swapping in a stand-in.

The lot is **101 real GameObjects** with per-car culling and LODGroups, not an InstancedMesh — the same seeded layout as the web build (`Mulberry32` in `uint`), paint as 18 generated materials so the instancing survives.

The interior is a teleport cell with a fog/ambient swap; its lights stay on and the sun stays up, both of which the web build only fights because of Three's forward renderer.

**Caught:** `tesla.glb` / `avenger.glb` require `EXT_texture_webp` and glTFast rejects the whole file (`tools/glb-webp-to-png.py`); and a BoxCollider that ignores model scale is a kilometre wide on the 37.4× Avenger.

cards.name: U14 — Map + minimap, as a live second camera
cards.desc:
The base layer is a **live second camera into a 1024² RenderTexture**, not the web's boot-time bake — no readback, no shader-compile spike, and moving cars show. Both states capped at 12 fps; the web caps only the minimap.

UI Toolkit arrives eleven units before U25: `MapView` paints outlines/dots/arrow with Painter2D and pools `Label`s, `GameMap` owns the panel and the `M` toggle, `MapRegistry` ports `world/registry.ts` and is the hook missions add objective pins to.

**Caught:** `PlaceSpec` has no `name` in `config.ts` — the pin labels live in `map-pois.ts`, and reading the absent field crashed the label pass; and a 16-bit RT depth makes Metal log "memoryless depth surface" as an *error*.

The minimap was removed and restored on the same day, both on the user's call. The removal built the mechanism the restore keeps: with the radar off and the map closed, the whole second-camera pass is **skipped** rather than rendered into a texture nobody sees.

cards.name: U15 — World memory: the textures were never compressed
cards.desc:
**The rule "can Unity do this better?" has to be allowed to answer *not like that*, and this is the unit that proves it.** The planned answer was Addressables; the measurement rejected it — 13.5 GB of scene memory, 96% textures, and streaming 13.5 GB in chunks is still 13.5 GB.

The real cause was a format nothing had ever set: **glTFast textures are `.glb` sub-assets with no TextureImporter**, so nothing ever compressed them — 12.9 GB of raw RGB24.

**The Block → Compress Textures** slices the embedded PNG/JPEGs verbatim out of the GLB container, and a custom importer makes the *first* import BC1/BC7 with settings derived from the file **name**, so a Library wipe cannot lose them. 688 material slots rebound.

**Scene texture memory 13,498 → 3,204 MB (4.2×).** Caught: texture names are not unique inside a `.glb` (seven "Untitled" in city 4), so the resolver matches name + size + alpha and refuses to guess; and NPOT + mips silently skips block compression while the importer claims DXT1.
checklist: 2026-08-15 11:04 · 4b7a93d · the world's textures were never compressed, and now they are

Placement is `npc.config.ts` verbatim, now **exported rather than re-typed**: the exporter gained a second source. 687 baked + 460 runtime positions.

cards.name: U17 + U17b — Traffic: graph, cars, lights, and the carjack

**How many cars is measured, not chosen:** 130 cars over 12,759 m of network, read off the web build's own config and applied per metre of street in range. **U17b:** `E` resolves three ways in `main.ts`'s own order — real vehicle → parked filler (101 of them) → stopped street car, which waits 5 s for you. Both swaps measured rather than eyeballed: the carjack lands at **0.000 m / 0.00°**. The enabler is that every car prefab now shares one origin — body centre in XZ, contact patch in Y.

**Two lamp faults, and neither was the state machine:** the lamp quads were built 14 cm *inside* the housing, and then the lenses turned out to be **wound inside-out** — grey head-on, coloured from the side. Winding hides geometry, not position.

cards.name: U19 — Police pursuit over a real street graph
cards.desc:
**The sharpest "design intent carries, scar tissue does not" call in the port.** The web build's *"cops drive straight at you, all routing deleted"* was forced by a graph split into five disconnected islands — not a design choice. Here it is **real A\* over a stitched view of U17's graph**; stitching T-junctions within 3 m makes 97.9% of the city one component. Straight-line survives in exactly two places.

**It also took four follow-up rows, and the first is the ledger's most-quoted lesson.** U19 shipped a better continuous wanted meter *and* "cruisers park at the station" (a 15–60 s travel time) in the same unit. Each was right; together they were a pursuit that could not happen, because the star died in six seconds. **When a unit adds a duration, put every clock next to it.**

Later rounds: traffic yields to a pursuit instead of walling it (a kinematic traffic car is a wall to a 1400 kg dynamic body); a blue-light run so a cop does not queue at a red; and finally an officer who **drives** the cruiser and gets out to arrest you on foot — the user's own design, not a port.

cards.name: U22 — M2: the beach dance, on the DSP clock
cards.desc:
✅ User-confirmed 2026-08-16. **The biggest feel win in the whole tier, and it is one line of engine difference:** the clock is `AudioSettings.dspTime`.

The web reads `audioElement.currentTime` — main thread, quantised to the decode buffer, jittering against the frame. Against 50 ms judgment windows on a build with a 42 ms frame, that is scoring the frame rate instead of the player. **Measured drift here: 0.02 ms** over a full run.

**The unit's scar, and it is a Unity feature having a price nobody quoted:** putting the song on a mixer bus is plainly right — it is what a Music slider attaches to — and it inserted **one DSP buffer, 21.3 ms, 43% of a Perfect window**, between the beatmap's anchor and the speakers. Nothing broke and nothing logged. It was caught only because U22 had written its drift number down and re-measured after the change.

**450 MB → 34 MB:** nine Mixamo with-skin FBX imported for their clips only, then deleted — the LFS budget is shared with the other repo.

Two owings, paid by two later units. **The fade** behind U13's interior teleport — it *covers* rather than brackets, black up in the same frame as the teleport.

**And the emoji font, which landed with U28.** `EmojiFontBuilder` builds NotoColorEmoji (OFL) as a dynamic `FontAsset` at `GlyphRenderMode.COLOR` — **the render mode is the whole question**, because CBDT/CBLC glyphs are bitmaps and every SDF mode rasterises them empty. Until then the ledger's standing instruction had been "strip the emoji from mission copy". That rule is now superseded.

cards.name: U26 — The shell: boot bar, title, roster, pause, settings
cards.desc:
✅ User-confirmed 2026-08-16. A Boot scene whose bar reads **`AsyncOperation.progress`** — the number `loading-screen.ts` wished for and had to fake with hand-counted milestones — then a title screen over the frozen city: New Game · Continue · Character · Mission Select · Settings · How to Play, plus `Esc` → Resume / Settings / How to Play / Quit to Title.

The character preview is a **second camera into a RenderTexture**, rather than the second WebGL context that *"did not hold on an iPad"*.

**⚠ The unit's real lesson: `Time.timeScale = 0` does not stop `Update`.** The web pauses by skipping one `stepSim` call; here fourteen scripts poll the keyboard every frame and kept firing behind the overlay, so `Core.Pause.Frozen` is a guard line in each of them. **The dance is unpausable by rule** — `Conductor` runs on `dspTime`, which no freeze touches.

cards.name: U27 — Audio: sfx, engine, ambient, 3D sirens
cards.desc:
✅ User-confirmed 2026-08-16. Twelve of the web's thirteen audio modules, ~1.2 MB of clips, one `AudioMixer` (7 buses / 7 exposed params / 4 snapshots) built by a **reflection tool**, because Unity ships no public API for authoring a mixer.

The 20 synth cues of `sfx.ts` are **baked to `AudioClip`s once** instead of rebuilding an oscillator graph per press, with PolyBLEP on saw/square because Web Audio's oscillators are band-limited by spec and a naive one would alias audibly.

The rotor is a literal port through `OnAudioFilterRead` — its three rates move by different factors (2.43× / 1.71× / 2.17×), so one `pitch` knob cannot reproduce it.

**Sirens are 3D, on the cars, capped at the nearest 3.** The web's single constant-gain wail exists only because that build has no `AudioListener` in it at all.

✅ User-confirmed 2026-08-16 — *"looking good"*. Joe, Jody and David.

**This is U9 paying a dividend on a unit built four months earlier.** The web build's `applyCharacter` has to reach **five** separately-built skinned rigs — walking capsule, seated driver, bike rider, jetski rider — and its own comment says why: *"picking one has to reach all of them or you'd change clothes on getting into a vehicle"*. cards.name: U33 — Day/night cycle, shipped switched off
cards.desc:
✅ User-confirmed 2026-08-16 — *"i like the lighting"*. **Settings → Display → Time of Day**, default **Fixed**. Day length 2880 s = 48 real minutes, GTA V's own pace, the user's call after playing the 24-minute version.

**The rule this unit sets, and it governs every addition after it: an addition ships switched OFF, and its off state is the old behaviour *replayed*, not neutral values fed through the new code path.** `DayNightCycle` does not write a neutral sky when off — it does not write at all, URP schedules no post pass, and every screenshot approved in U11–U27 still reproduces.

**One light does the sun and the moon** — URP's main light is the brightest directional and a second would demote to an additional light with no shadows — so it swings a full 360° and mirrors below the horizon. **Ambient is `Trilight`, never `DynamicGI.UpdateEnvironment`** (1–3 ms per re-convolution). **Night is cheaper than day:** below the horizon the four 2048² shadow cascades drop.

⚠ This row was corrected: it once claimed to be the first thing the port *adds*. The original has a day/night cycle at `enabled: false`. What is true is the narrower claim — in the *shipped* web build the sun never moves.

cards.name: U34 — Collisions have consequences
cards.desc:
✅ User-confirmed 2026-08-16.

**The unit exists because of one discovery: `CrashSensor` had been attached to nothing since U19** — no prefab, no scene object, no `AddComponent` anywhere — so `CrimeWatch.OnCrashed` and the crash thump were both subscribed to an event that could not fire. **Every collision in this game had been silent and free for fourteen units.**

It was found by grepping the `.meta` **guid** rather than the class name, which is the only search that distinguishes "referenced" from "merely compiled".

The fix is `CrashSensor.Ensure(gameObject)` called from `Bind` — deliberately **not** a prefab field, because `Build Drivable Cars` regenerates those prefabs and that is the likeliest story of how it was lost to begin with.
checklist: 2026-08-16 17:23 · 9bd360c · collisions have consequences

cards.name: U35a — Ragdolls: the crowd and the player
cards.desc:
✅ User-confirmed 2026-08-16. `Build Ragdolls` writes 11 bodies / 10 joints / ~64 kg into six pedestrians and three player characters. **Settings → Gameplay → Ragdolls**, default on.

**Three faults building it, all now memory files:** `Optimize Game Objects` deletes the very bones a ragdoll needs; `Interpolate` on a kinematic body writes PhysX onto the transform, so a resting rig smears the whole crowd to the prefab pose; and a kinematic body's PhysX pose is **stale** when it goes dynamic, so it teleports to the prefab pose on activation.

The bike throw → dismount → stand up → remount loop was played and confirmed the same day.

cards.name: U35b — Vehicle damage: dents, smoke, fire, shed parts
cards.desc:
✅ User-confirmed 2026-08-16. Three layers behind **Settings → Gameplay → Vehicle Damage**, default off, with a fuse.

**Three findings:** the Mustang is eighteen *skinned* meshes whose vertices live in bind space, so a dent has to rebuild `bone[i].localToWorld * bindposes[i]` per use; **the contact normal points INTO the struck body**, so the first dent bulged the nose outward by 0.136 m; and the `.glb`s group by **material**, which is why layer ③ needed no Blender pass and why the Mustang alone sheds nothing — it has no bumper node to detach.

Two additions the user asked for mid-play-test, both landed: **a wrecked car cannot be entered and the player is told why** — through U28's existing `EntryRefusal` socket, on the same HUD line that offers the key. One predicate feeds both the prompt and the key.

cards.name: U35h — Breakable street props
cards.desc:
✅ User-confirmed 2026-08-18 — *"looking good"*.

**The user asked the right question first** — *is there an option to take assets that already exist in the game, like the traffic light or a bench, and make them breakable?* — and it was **measured against the tree rather than guessed**. The answer is half good news: the **233 traffic-light poles are separate GameObjects with their own colliders and are a free win**, and benches, bins and bollards do not exist as objects at all — they are baked into the district meshes.

So the user supplied three Sketchfab props, which went through a **headless Blender prep** (`tools/prep-props.sh`) rather than a hand pass. Sketchfab scale varies per model — the cone's accessor claimed 0.29 m and the baked mesh was 29 m.

Benches were re-sited onto the crowd strips after the first play-test put them in the carriageway. Sleeping props need an `Awake`-time `Sleep()`: a physics step fits between Instantiate and Start.

cards.name: U30b — Perf campaign, measured on the Player and not the Editor
cards.desc:
**Four rounds, and its best result is a list of things that turned out not to matter.**

**R1 —** resident texture memory **1213 → 331 MB**, hitches **46 → 2**.

**R2 — the frame is bound by GEOMETRY, not memory and not pixels.** A 16× resolution cut moves it 11 ms out of 78, so `renderScale`, shadow quality and probe settings are all the wrong place to spend. 7,899 draw calls and 21.9 M triangles at the parking lot. The jetski was 1.19 M triangles with no LODGroup, and the scene has two — fixed to 210,850, and the pair went from 8.98 M drawn triangles to 1.83 M. **Kept only because it passed a close-range pixel diff at 0.900% against a 0.000% noise floor; the first attempt did not pass and was reverted.**

**R3 — the deltas were measured by a machine**, 44 unattended Player launches, one per configuration. Six of eight showcase features cost **nothing measurable**. The census then found something never on any list: **the 101 parked lot cars are 4.28 M triangles — 43% of the world, +8.1 ms.** One parked Tesla is 52,096 triangles.

**R4 —** occlusion culling baked and **proved free**; the parked cars proved **not** decimatable; and the scene turned out to have **no real LODs at all** — all 334 LODGroups are `lodCount 1`.

**The campaign's own rule: freeze the world to measure anything.** A live crowd has no steady state, so "below the noise floor" there means the measurement never happened.

cards.name: U36 — The sea is a place, not a wall
cards.desc:
✅ User-confirmed 2026-08-18. Sand that reads as sand, and a GTA-style water entry.

**The "black strip" on the beach was not a colour problem at all — it was the shader rendering with NO SUN.** `TheBlock/Beach` declares `_SCREEN_SPACE_OCCLUSION`, this renderer runs SSAO with **Source = DepthNormals**, and the shader had **no DepthNormals pass** — so it wrote nothing into `_CameraNormalsTexture`, the AO resolve read garbage under its own pixels, and the sand kept its albedo while losing the sun. Measured, not guessed: the albedo was already correct gold.

The second half was the user's other report: **driving into the water should not call the police.** It never did — *the wall did*. An invisible shore collider was reading as a game rule.

**The user's ask — *"we need more ways for our character to make money"* — named a real gap, not a nice-to-have:** every campaign payout is once-per-run through `Payouts`, while power-ups, paint, fuel and fines all keep charging. A cleared campaign was a wallet that could only go down.

cards.name: U38 — A crowd of strangers: 12 bodies × 30 looks
cards.desc:
✅ User-confirmed 2026-08-19. Twelve pack bodies at 360 distinct looks — **and it made the frame roughly 22 ms FASTER.**

That is the whole point of the row: the six Mixamo pedestrians U16b shipped are **~50k triangles each**, and the pack bodies are **11× lighter**. More variety and less cost, at the same time.

**Two measurement traps caught here:** skinned bounds are the *clip's sweep*, not the body — 1.968 m of bounds on a 1.769 m body had been building the whole crowd 15% short; and `Face %` modulo silently hides extra prefabs, so six baked face values into a twelve-long list uses the first six and says nothing.

Also: the ground plate is **three** objects, and an exact-name test had put 16% of the crowd 16 cm underground.

✅ Falafel half user-confirmed 2026-08-19.

**① The orphan stand:** a second complete falafel stand (7 renderers, 41,098 tris) had been sitting at the world origin since `154954e`, invisible to the cleanup sweep because it carried the raw asset name instead of `Place_FalafelStand`. Deleted; the sweep now matches the model file's name too. Exactly −41,098 triangles.

**② The lane through it:** pedestrians have no `NavMeshAgent`, so they follow authored `LanePath`s and carving the NavMesh would do nothing. One path ran straight through the stand's footprint. **⚠ Detouring per *point* fails** — a polyline is its segments, so a moved sample beside an unmoved one leaves a diagonal cutting back through the building. `DetourRuns` offsets a whole padded run and re-resamples.

cards.name: U30c — Ship hardening: strip the debug keys
cards.desc:
**Deliberately last, and deliberately AFTER the video is recorded** — `P`, `T`, `C`, `PowerUps.debugStock` and Mission Select are how a five-minute recording reaches every feature in the game. Strip them before recording and the video cannot be made.

What comes out or gets gated: `CrimeWatch.debugStarKey` (`P`, currently `true` and serialized in the scene, i.e. **it ships today**), U17's `T`, U16's `C`, `PowerUps.debugStock`, `CampaignRunner.debugStartMission`.

One judgement call rather than a deletion: `Wallet.startingBalance` is 500 here against the web's 0, and it is rewritten by every `Build Store` / `Build World` run — so "fix it in the scene" is not a fix.

cards.name: Record the 5-minute submission video (Unity build)
cards.desc:
Requirements #3, #4 and #6 of the brief, all in one recording: the idea name + one-liner · the list of major features implemented · **the whole project running, all features, at good resolution** — recorded from `Builds/macOS-dev/The Block.app`, not the Editor.

**The video's central argument is the pivot itself.** It has to answer *"why change engines mid-project?"*, and the Tier 8 additions are the evidence: they were chosen against a rule — *the web build could not have done it* — rather than collected. Real A\* pursuit against five disconnected graph islands; Rigidbody wrecks against a 30-vehicle Rapier budget; `dspTime` against `audioElement.currentTime`.

It must also state which features were **invented** and which were **ported** — and be accurate about it. The day/night row was corrected in the ledger precisely because it was the source for that claim.

cards.name: The architecture diagram — Unity's, not the web one relabelled
cards.desc:
Requirement #5: a diagram of the APIs / tools / libraries used, with the flow — what calls what, and when. **The Three.js diagram will not do; this is a different inventory.**

Unity's: URP · glTFast · Draco · Splines · AI Navigation · Input System · UI Toolkit · TextCore emoji `FontAsset` · AudioMixer · PlayerPrefs.

Plus the arrow this project should be proudest of, which has no counterpart in the original: **the offline pipeline** — `config.ts` → `export-config.mjs` → `theblock-config.json` → `WorldBuilder` → baked `ScriptableObject`s (traffic graph, route graph, roof spots, NavMesh). The runtime casts no rays for any of it.

The tool side is worth its own arrow too: MCP for Unity drives the Editor, and Blender MCP built the H145, the auto shop and the falafel stand.

cards.name: Upload the video to Google Drive, anyone-with-link
cards.desc: Requirement #7. The link goes in the moodle PDF, so sharing has to be **anyone with the link can view** — a Drive file left on "restricted" reads as a missing submission.

cards.name: Write the moodle submission PDF
cards.desc:
Requirement #8, one PDF holding three things: the Google Drive link to the video (anyone-with-link) · the GitHub repo links · the **final screenshot of this board**.

Both repos are listed, because the pivot is presented rather than hidden:

- Phase 1, Three.js — https://github.com/RoeeSivan/Finalproject
- Phase 2, Unity — https://github.com/RoeeSivan/theblock-unity

cards.name: Zip the Unity source as `finalproject.zip`
cards.desc:
Requirement #9. **The recipe is measured and it is not the obvious answer.** A whole-tree zip is 1.66 GiB across 1,262 tracked files — no moodle takes that.

But `Assets/Scripts` + `Assets/Editor` + `ProjectSettings` + `Packages` + `tools` + the two `.md` files is **898 KB / 427 files**, and that *is* the source: the 2.2 GB in `Assets/Models` is third-party art. Measured 2026-08-16.

cards.name: Keep pushing to the repo through to 1 Oct
cards.desc:
Requirement #1 is graded on commits **throughout**, not on a repo that appears finished on the deadline. The instructor is invited to both repos as of 2026-08-19, so everything that lands from here is visible.

**⚠ The real constraint is LFS bandwidth, not storage.** 150 objects / 1.30 GiB are already on the remote and nothing is missing — but the free tier is **1 GiB per month, per account, shared with `Finalproject`**. One clone by the instructor pulls ~1.3 GiB and can exhaust the month for **both** repos. Check the budget before adding any large asset.

cards.name: U32 — Multiplayer in Unity
cards.desc:
Deferred to the last unit since U0 and never scheduled. The Three.js build has Supabase Realtime broadcast + presence; nothing of it is ported.

Not a gap the submission needs closed — it was ranked last on purpose, and the port's remaining time belongs to the video, the board and the zip.

cards.name: ⏸ U31 — iOS / iPad
cards.desc:
**Dropped by the user 2026-08-16** — *"iPad is not relevant to the submission."* Out of scope, not failed and not deferred: the port ships to **macOS**, full stop.

This changes no design decision retroactively — iPad was always ranked "a wanted bonus, never a constraint on design" — it only stops future units paying a tax for a platform nobody will run.

**What it does NOT license: ripping out iOS support.** The module is installed, `PlayerSettings` has an iOS section, and unused touch input costs nothing. Deleting any of it would be work spent making a future retry harder.

cards.name: ❌ U35d — Weather: rain, wet roads, lightning
cards.desc:
**Dropped by the user 2026-08-17** — *"the weather feature, take it down, it doesn't interest me any more."*

**Never started — no `Weather.cs`, no emitter, no scene object, nothing to rip out.** It was also the row this ledger itself had called *"the one most likely to fail the performance rule"* against a 20.7 ms frame, so the cut removes the largest un-measured perf risk left in Tier 8. The cut agrees with the selection rule rather than fighting it.

The argument it lost: rain that changes how the car *drives* — a `WheelFrictionCurve` whose stiffness drops with wetness is a physics engine doing the work, and visuals alone the web could fake.

cards.name: ❌ U35e — Stunt jumps + a Cinemachine camera
cards.desc:
**Dropped by the user 2026-08-17** — *"we decided we do not need that, so do not mention it again."* Nothing was built, so the cut costs no work, and with it **Tier 8 had no scheduled unit left**.

It had already been re-scoped once the day before: the **skid marks were cut** by the user, and the handbrake went with them, since it existed to make the marks worth drawing.

cards.name: ❌ U35f — Side jobs: taxi and deliveries in free roam
cards.desc:
**Dropped by the user 2026-08-16.** The cut agrees with the ledger's own assessment: this was written down as **the weakest row against the selection rule** — the one whose argument was *design, not engine*.

The free-roam earning gap it was going to close stayed open, and that was a known and accepted state rather than an oversight — **until U37 closed it anyway**, two days later, with the falafel round the user asked for directly.

cards.name: ❌ GPS route line on the map
cards.desc:
**Built, then removed by the user in the same message that confirmed the helicopter it shipped with** — *"take the light-blue line off the map, we don't need this feature."*

**Deleted rather than defaulted off:** `GpsRoute.cs`, `MapView.SetRoute`/`DrawRoute`, `Progress.GpsRouteOn`, the Settings row and `MapRegistry.NearestGuide` are all gone. `RoutePlanner` / `RouteGraph` stay — **the police drive on them**.

cards.name: ❌ Car radio (not ported)
cards.desc:
**Dropped, not held** — *"radio: take it down too, it's not that important."* The Three.js build ships one (see its own Done card); the Unity port deliberately does not.

There was a technical finding underneath it: **FMOD cannot play an endless stream** — bytes flow at full bitrate and `audioClip` stays null — so a live-station radio was never going to be the cheap port it looked like.

cards.name: ❌ LOD1 for the 101 parked lot cars — cannot be built
cards.desc:
**An honest null result, and it is measured rather than argued.** After the perf census named the parked lot cars as the single biggest item in the world — 4.28 M triangles, 43% of it, +8.1 ms — the user asked for a decimated LOD1. **It does not exist to switch to.**

**Why:** Blender's COLLAPSE **tears these car bodies apart below ~80%** of their triangles (and normals are not the cause); **PLANAR does nothing on them**, because the 1° row says whether an asset is filler or curvature and the lot cars are curvature; and there is **no interior to drop**, because the `.glb`s group by material rather than by part.

**What did come out of it: three real bugs in the LOD arithmetic**, all of which had been shipping since U17 wearing an assert that could not fail. `lodBias` multiplies the screen height, so dividing by it lands the switch `lodBias²` too far; `LODGroup.size` is local space and is 1 until `SetLODs` runs, which had a scale-37 car culling at 1,685 m.

**And the finding that made the whole item moot: the lot cars cost nothing outside the lot.** 10.8 M triangles when you stand in it, zero from the city.
